{{Short description|Order-independent convergence of a sequence}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[functional analysis]], a series is '''unconditionally convergent''' if all reorderings of the series converge to the same value. In contrast, a series is [[conditional convergence|conditionally convergent]] if it converges but different orderings do not all converge to that same value. Unconditional convergence is equivalent to [[absolute convergence]] in [[Dimension (vector space)|finite-dimensional]] [[vector space]]s, but is a weaker property in infinite dimensions.

==Definition==

Let <math>X</math> be a [[topological vector space]]. Let <math>I</math> be an [[index set]] and <math>x_i \in X</math> for all <math>i \in I.</math>

The series <math>\textstyle \sum_{i \in I} x_i</math> is called '''unconditionally convergent''' to  <math>x \in X,</math> if
* the indexing set <math>I_0 := \left\{i \in I : x_i \neq 0\right\}</math> is [[countable]], and
* for every [[permutation]] ([[bijection]]) <math>\sigma : I_0 \to I_0</math> of <math>I_0 = \left\{i_k\right\}_{k=1}^\infty</math> the following relation holds: <math>\sum_{k=1}^\infty x_{\sigma\left(i_k\right)} = x.</math>

==Alternative definition==
Unconditional convergence is often defined in an equivalent way: A series is unconditionally convergent if for every sequence <math>\left(\varepsilon_n\right)_{n=1}^\infty,</math> with <math>\varepsilon_n \in \{-1, +1\},</math> the series
<math display=block>\sum_{n=1}^\infty \varepsilon_n x_n</math>
converges.

If <math>X</math> is a [[Banach space]], every [[absolute convergence|absolutely convergent]] series is unconditionally convergent, but the [[Converse (logic)|converse]] implication does not hold in general. Indeed, if <math>X</math> is an infinite-dimensional Banach space, then by [[Absolute convergence#Rearrangements and unconditional convergence|Dvoretzky&ndash;Rogers theorem]] there always exists an unconditionally convergent series in this space that is not absolutely convergent. However, when <math>X = \R^n,</math> by the [[Riemann series theorem]], the series <math display=inline>\sum_n x_n</math> is unconditionally convergent if and only if it is absolutely convergent.
